chapter: Tenor players, tours and band boys
title: Broadway bombs, Mitch Miller TV and the Ed Sullivan show with Cab
summary: He lists three failed Broadway shows, Sing Along With Mitch Miller, and Ed Sullivan appearances with Cab's four-piece band.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well, I don't think you missed anybody from what it says here, unless they hadn't come along yet, Panama. We were talking about all those studio recordings you did, and I see where you did a few Broadway shows, too.
"Marathon '33."
Yeah, but all of them were bombs. I think I'm the only guy in the world who got three bombs in a row.
"The Fantastics" -- "West Side Story" made it, though.
Yeah, but that was in a little theatre out in California.
Oh, so that was a small "West Side Story," then.
It was a small "West Side Story," but I mean the big Broadway shows, I had three bombs.
Well, you can't win them all! Of course, you did that "Sing Along With Mitch Miller," the television show.
Oh, yeah, I did that show for a year and a half.
And then you did some things with the Jackie Gleason Show, you did those; and of course, you made appearances with different artists on the Ed Sullivan Show.
Yeah.
And that was THE television show in New York.
Yes, it was. Well, you know, we did the Ed Sullivan Show with Cab, with the four pieces.
Uh huh. You know, I had forgotten that.
That's right. We did it at the Roxy, I think -- that's when he first started out with the four pieces, with Cab.
Uh huh.

And then we did it again when they moved to the theatre on 41st Street off of Sixth Avenue when they were doing his show from there then at the time, and we did it with Cab -- I think we were there twice with Cab.
Hey, that was way back when the world was young ...
Oh, my gracious -- that was when he first started out.
Right. That must have been Dumont.
That's right, it sure was.
Besides that, and all this recording and all the other things you'd done, plus the nightclubs you played with: Slim Gaillard and Della Reese and who else here?
Oh, Dinah Shore, Polly Bergen, Paul Anka, George Maharis, Joe Williams ...
